quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Put the car in neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when:

options.text: Your windshield wipers cannot clear the rain.
Your tires lose contact with the road.
Spray from a large truck blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: When driving fast on wet roads, your tires can ride on a layer of water instead of touching the pavement. This is hydroplaning. It can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to get better traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Even at 30 mph in heavy rain, your tires can lose grip and ride on water. If this happens, slow down slowly. Do not use the brakes.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds mean you need more following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 mph, survival is almost impossible. Higher speeds also increase stopping distance, so increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: In rain, be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has rained all day.
A half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping in the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with rain to make the road slippery.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot dangers early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for merging vehicles and sudden changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead as during the day, and oncoming headlights create glare. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be alert for children riding bikes on sidewalks who may suddenly enter the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign alerts drivers that the right lane is ending. Be ready for merging traffic.

questions.question: In fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare that makes it harder to see ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does "BAC" mean?

options.text: Blood alcohol concentration.
Big alcohol content.
Blood alcohol conservation.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. Drivers age 21 or older are driving under the influence when their BAC is 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: Looking far ahead on the highway helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic.
Avoid sudden braking or turning.
Spot police officers.

questions.explanation: Look far ahead to avoid last-minute stops or turns. This helps you drive safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic. Only turn left when it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: All work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides of a divided highway.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for green before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and go carefully.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may pass unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may pass unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is risky. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, what will most likely happen?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
You will help traffic flow better.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You should drive at the same speed as other traffic unless that speed is above the legal limit. Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can block traffic flow and result in a ticket.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that traffic will be merging from the right. Be ready to let other cars merge safely into your lane.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop completely. Just make sure it is safe before you proceed.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in your blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood as a percentage. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, other drivers may not see you. What should you turn on?

options.text: Your dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever visibility is poor or when other drivers cannot see you. Always use your low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.
